item.title: AWS Simplifies WAF Pricing with Three-Dimensional Model
item.description:
AWS Simplifies WAF Pricing with Three-Dimensional Model

📊 Overview

Starting today, AWS WAF pricing is easier to predict. Your bill is now based on three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply to that traffic. For new or smaller workloads, the Free plan of CloudFront flat-rate pricing plans is another way to start. If your application serves fewer than 1 million requests per month, the Free plan costs $0 per month for each CloudFront distribution. It includes AWS WAF protection against common web threats, DDoS protection, and the CloudFront CDN, with no overage charges.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Adding a protection (such as a rule, Bot Control, or Anti-DDoS rule group) no longer adds a subscription or a separate per-request charge. Those requests bill at the base request rate.
  • Capacity no longer affects your rate. Each protection pack (web ACL) now includes up to 2,500 web ACL capacity units (WCUs), up from 1,500, and going past your included capacity does not raise what you pay per request.
  • The premium request fee applies only to the traffic you choose to send through advanced protections.
  • You can estimate costs before writing a first rule, and those estimates hold even as your rules change.
  • Security rules change often. Adding, reordering, or removing rules does not change your rate.
  • For AWS Shield Advanced subscribers, nothing changes. Your Shield Advanced subscription, its price, and your included AWS WAF entitlement stay the same.
  • Customers on a CloudFront flat-rate pricing plan also see no change.

💰 How Costs Are Calculated

AWS WAF bills three fees:

Fee Type Description
Resource Fee Hourly charge for each resource associated with a protection pack (e.g., CloudFront distributions, Application Load Balancers, Amazon API Gateway APIs).
Base Request Fee Applies to each request AWS WAF inspects.
Premium Request Fee Applies on top of the base request fee, to requests evaluated by advanced protections like Bot Control, Fraud Control, API Security, and AI Security.

Both API Security and AI Security use the same premium request fee, with no separate subscription or rate. Requests evaluated by one or more advanced protections are billed $5.60 per million: the $0.60 base request fee plus the $5.00 premium request fee. AWS WAF charges the premium request fee once per request, however many advanced protections evaluate it. A request blocked before reaching an advanced protection pays only the base request fee.

🚀 Availability and Transition

  • Existing AWS WAF customers move to the new pricing on February 1, 2027. Until then, they keep their current pricing and don’t need to do anything at launch.
  • If you hold an AWS WAF private pricing agreement, it stays in force until it expires.
  • The new pricing includes the Security analytics dashboard, which shows full traffic metrics for your protected applications over a rolling 21-day window at no additional cost.

💡 Example: Cost Estimation

Here’s a worked example from the AWS WAF pricing page:

Example 1: One protected resource (Application Load Balancer) serving 20 million requests per month.

  • Resource fee: 1 resource × $0.01 per hour × 730 hours = $7.30
  • Base request fee: 20 million × $0.60 per million = $12.00
  • Total: $19.30 per month

For more pricing details and examples, visit the AWS WAF pricing page. If you have questions about how the new pricing applies to your account, contact your AWS account team or open a Support case.

#AWS #WAF #CloudSecurity #Pricing

Source: Introducing AWS WAF simplified pricing | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Google Announces Gemini 4 Neon – Pricing Confusion Deepens
item.description:
Google Announces Gemini 4 Neon – Pricing Confusion Deepens

Today Google introduced Gemini 4 Neon.

⚙️ Pricing

I wrote recently about how confusing the pricing for the Gemini 4 series was - Neon has somehow made this even worse.

Variant Input price per million Output price per million
Neon $3 $15
Carbon $2 $10
Hydrogen $1.50 $7.50
  • Carbon is currently half its future price.
  • Neon is the most expensive variant right now.

🧩 Lineup

The Neon announcement pretends that Argon doesn’t exist.

So the lineup now, from most to least expensive, is Carbon, Neon, Hydrogen.

Except Carbon is currently half price, so right now Neon ($3/million input, $15/million output) is the most expensive of the three - then Carbon ($2/$10), then Hydrogen ($1.50/$7.50).

I guess this will make more sense when Carbon doubles to $4/$20 on December 1st.

🎨 Prompt

I also fired the following prompt against Gemini 4 Neon on “extra” effort level in Google Antigravity:

1

Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data

📊 Comparison

I dropped Argon from my Gemini 4 comparison grid - here’s the new Gemini 4 lineup, where the Neon pelicans do look better than Hydrogen and worse than Carbon:

  • Neon pelicans look better than Hydrogen and worse than Carbon.

#Google #Gemini #AI #Pricing #Neon

Source: Release: llm-gemini 0.38

item.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with updated pricing
item.description:
OpenAI introduces GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with updated pricing

OpenAI has introduced two new frontier models: GPT-6.2 Astra, designed for the hardest projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, an efficient and versatile model for everyday work. These models are now available via API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, with support included in LLM 0.38.

🚀 Availability

The new models have been integrated into the OpenAI API and related developer tools:

  • Available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol.
  • Support was shipped in LLM 0.38.
  • The models can be accessed using the Codex CLI and Codex desktop app with “Ultra” effort levels.

⚙️ Key details

Pricing for the new models reflects significant discounts compared to their predecessors. GPT-6.2 Astra is priced at 80% of the cost of the previous 6 Astra model, while GPT-6.2 Sol maintains the same pricing structure as previous Sol versions.

Model Input Price (per MTok) Output Price (per MTok) Cached Price (per MTok)
GPT-6.2 Astra $8 $40 $0.40
GPT-6.2 Sol $2 $10 Not specified

Performance and User Experience

  • Benchmarks: GPT-6.2 Astra is not scoring quite as high as Claude Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks.
  • Coding Tasks: In a specific three.js animation task prompting a mech to stomp around Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn, neither GPT-6.2 Astra nor Sol performed as well as Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon in morphing Yonkers into a big mech.
  • Communication Style: Users have reported that GPT-6.2 Astra’s communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne noted that the model can pull in subagents and manage them well but may ask users “weird internal implementation detail” questions they cannot understand, such as asking if a specific reviewer writes clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4 while working on a game level.

#OpenAI #GPT-6.2 #API #Pricing #Benchmarks

Source: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol

item.title: Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model
item.description:
Meta AI launches Muse Ember, a small, efficient reasoning model

Meta AI just launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day.

🔍 Overview

  • Smallest and most efficient model in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category.
  • Targeted at tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.

🧩 How it works

  • Offers six reasoning levels: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max.
  • Visual examples include six pelicans riding bicycles, with the “max” level shown and others noted as comparable to Muse Wonder (40× the price of Ember).

⚙️ Key details

Model Input price (per M tokens) Output price (per M tokens) Token limit
Muse Ember $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
GPT‑6 Luna $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Haiku 5.5 $0.10 $0.50 Up to 1 M (price rises after a threshold)
Claude Fable 5.2 $8.00 $40.00 –
  • For shorter prompts Ember is priced the same as GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5.
  • Pricing becomes less straightforward as prompts get longer; after the threshold Ember’s price sits between Luna/Haiku and Claude Fable.

📊 Efficiency metrics

  • Artificial Analysis is highlighted as a useful measure.
  • The Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Task chart places Muse Ember on the Pareto line, where improving one dimension requires sacrificing another.
  • Meta notes Ember sits on the efficiency frontier of the full Artificial Analysis leaderboard: no model scores higher for less per task.
  • The grey dot on the Pareto line (mid‑green area) represents GPT‑6.1 Terra (low), noted as worth attention.

🚀 Availability

  • Muse Ember is available now with pricing identical to GPT‑6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 for short inputs.
  • Longer prompts trigger a price threshold, positioning Ember’s cost between the low‑price models and the higher‑priced Claude Fable 5.2.

#MetaAI #MuseEmber #AIModels #Pricing #ArtificialAnalysis

Source: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon model released with updated pricing structure
item.description:
Gemini 4 Argon model released with updated pricing structure

Support has been added to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model, which is now available via the Gemini API and for customers of the $100/month subscription plan.

⚙️ Key details

Argon exhibits strong performance in SVG generation, a capability noted in previous Gemini models. Testing shows the model can produce detailed illustrations, such as the “high” pelican SVG, at a cost of approximately 17.166 cents.

💰 Pricing

Pricing is set to increase on December 1st. Current and future rates are as follows:

Tier Input (per million) Output (per million) Status
Current Launch $2 $10 Available
Post-December 1st $4 $20 Scheduled

💡 Why it matters

While raw token pricing is one metric, the model’s efficiency in an agentic harness is considered more significant. Artificial Analysis reports that Argon costs $2,407 to run their benchmark, placing it close to GLM-5.3 and at a lower cost than current models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta.

#Gemini #LLM #AI #Pricing

Source: Release: llm-gemini 0.35

item.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API with image‑capable decision model
item.description:
OpenAI launches Decisions API with image‑capable decision model

OpenAI released its new Decisions API, a Jev‑style service announced at last week’s DevDay.

🔍 Overview

  • The Decisions API follows the same conceptual shape as the existing Jev service.
  • Announced during OpenAI’s DevDay.

🧩 How it works

  • Supports three question types: yes/no, multiple‑choice, and scoring.
  • Accepts text input; the gpt‑6‑luna decision model also accepts image input.
  • Charges are applied only to input tokens.

⚙️ Key details

  • Pricing: 10 ¢ per million input tokens for OpenAI; Jev charges 4.2 ¢ per million input tokens.
  • No fee for output tokens.
  • A plugin (llm‑openai‑decisions) can be installed; the README shows the install command.
  • The README includes an example query against an image attachment and the corresponding example output.

🚀 Availability

  • The service was announced at last week’s DevDay and is available via the new plugin.

#OpenAI #DecisionsAPI #LLM #ImageInput #Pricing

Source: Release: llm-openai-decisions 0.1a0

item.title: Anthropic and OpenAI Unveil Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT‑6 Models with Aggressive Pricing
item.description:
Anthropic and OpenAI Unveil Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT‑6 Models with Aggressive Pricing

Today Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, and within an hour OpenAI released GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna.

🔍 Overview

  • Claude Opus 5.5 arrives with a 20 % price reduction to $4 / $20 per million input/output tokens.
  • OpenAI introduced two GPT‑6 variants: Sol and Luna, both priced significantly lower than their GPT‑5.6 predecessors.
  • GPT‑6 Luna is priced at one tenth of the current Haiku 4.5 pricing ($1 / $5).
  • Claude Opus 5.5 supports a maximum output of 128,000 tokens.

⚙️ Pricing Details

Model Input ($/M tokens) Output ($/M tokens)
GPT‑6 Luna 0.10 0.50
GPT‑5.6 Luna 0.20 1.20
Grok 4.7 2 6
GPT‑6 Sol 2 10
GPT‑5.6 Terra 2 12
Claude Opus 5.5 4 20
GPT‑5.6 Sol 4 20
Claude Fable 5.1 10 50
GPT‑6 Astra 10 50
GPT‑4.1 Nano 0.10 0.40
GPT‑5 Nano 0.05 0.40

📊 Comparison

  • At $0.10 / $0.50, GPT‑6 Luna is among the cheapest OpenAI models, beaten only by the weaker GPT‑4.1 Nano and GPT‑5 Nano.
  • GPT‑6 Sol’s $2 / $10 pricing is half the promotional price of GPT‑5.6 Sol ($4 / $20).
  • Grok 4.7’s $2 / $6 pricing is less than half of GPT‑5.6 Sol and now matches GPT‑6 Sol on input cost.
  • GPT‑6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 share the same $10 / $50 pricing tier.

🚀 Availability

  • Both Anthropic and OpenAI announced their new models on the same day, with Claude Opus 5.5 released first and GPT‑6 Sol and Luna following within an hour.
  • Anthropic indicated that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are slated for future release.

#Anthropic #OpenAI #Pricing #LLM

Source: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and a new price war
